records.summary: Claude Code reads a stack of JSON settings files. Highest precedence first: managed settings, the --settings CLI value, .claude/settings.local.json, .claude/settings.json, then ~/.claude/settings.json. Scalar keys override; most array keys such as permissions.allow merge across scopes. Environment variables are not a level in the stack; each env var / settings key pair has its own documented winner.
details: Precedence (highest first): 1 managed (managed-settings.json, MDM plist, HKLM registry, or server-managed settings from claude.ai console); 2 --settings <file-or-json>; 3 .claude/settings.local.json; 4 .claude/settings.json; 5 ~/.claude/settings.json.

Managed tier internal order: server-managed settings > MDM/OS policy (macOS com.anthropic.claudecode plist, Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode value 'Settings') > managed-settings.json merged with managed-settings.d/*.json (alphabetical) > HKCU registry. By default only the highest-ranked managed source is read.

Managed file locations: macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/, Linux and WSL /etc/claude-code/, Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\. Same directory also holds managed-mcp.json, CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills/, .claude/agents/.
Lists merge instead of overriding (e.g. permissions.allow, sandbox.filesystem arrays). Exceptions: fallbackModel is taken whole from the highest file; a managed availableModels list is applied as-is.

Security-sensitive exceptions where a stricter lower-level value wins over managed: remoteControlAtStartup=false, crossSessionInbound (stricter), useAutoModeDuringPlan=false, syncClaudeAiSkills=false, syncClaudeAiPlugins=false; deny permission rules at any level cannot be overridden by allow at another level.

Env vars: ANTHROPIC_MODEL beats the model key from any file; ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL applies only when no file sets model. A settings-file env block value overrides the same variable exported in the shell. To neutralize an inherited variable, set it to "" in env.

CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR relocates ~/.claude (settings, sessions, plugins). ~/.claude.json is a separate 'global config' file holding OAuth account, UI state, per-project trust, and local/user-scoped MCP servers; 'Global config' keys apply only from it.

Claude Code writes .claude/settings.local.json when you choose 'Yes, and don't ask again' and adds **/.claude/settings.local.json to the global git excludes file the first time it writes it; hand-created files must be gitignored manually. The file is read/written at the git repo root (main checkout for worktrees).

Keys with scope 'User, local, or managed', 'User or managed', or 'Managed' never apply from the committed project file (e.g. defaultMode auto/bypassPermissions must be in user settings; autoMode is user or managed).

--setting-sources user,project,local limits which sources load; --restricted ignores user/project/local files; --bare and --safe-mode disable most customization. In -p mode invalid settings files are silently skipped.
Settings files reload live; ConfigChange hook fires per settings-file change with matcher user_settings|project_settings|local_settings|policy_settings|skills.
Cloud sessions read only committed .claude/settings.json and server-managed settings; user and local files are not read.

records.summary: CLAUDE.md files are concatenated into context at launch in load order: managed policy, user (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), then every CLAUDE.md / .claude/CLAUDE.md / CLAUDE.local.md from the filesystem root down to the working directory. Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files load lazily when Claude touches a file there. .claude/rules/*.md splits instructions into topic files, optionally path-scoped. AGENTS.md is read in place of CLAUDE.md when no CLAUDE.md exists (v2.1.277+).
details: Load order: managed CLAUDE.md -> ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md -> ancestor-to-cwd CLAUDE.md files (root first, cwd last); within a directory CLAUDE.local.md appends after CLAUDE.md. Files concatenate; they do not override.
Subdirectory CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md below cwd load on demand when Claude reads, writes, or edits a file in that subdirectory (including cat/head via Bash).

@path/to/file imports: relative to the containing file, recursive up to 4 hops, skipped inside backticks/code fences, spaces escaped with backslash, quoted paths not imported. Imports resolving outside the working directory in project files trigger a one-time approval dialog; user-scope imports are trusted.

.claude/rules/: all .md files discovered recursively; without 'paths' frontmatter they load at launch with the same priority as .claude/CLAUDE.md; with 'paths:' (glob list or comma string) they load only when Claude touches a matching file. 'paths' is the only frontmatter key read. Symlinks supported; symlinks outside the working dir count as external imports. ~/.claude/rules/ applies to all projects and loads before project rules.

Managed CLAUDE.md: /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md (macOS), /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md (Linux/WSL), C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md; cannot be excluded by users. Alternatively the 'claudeMd' string key in managed-settings.json (managed scope only).
claudeMdExcludes setting (path or glob) skips specific ancestor CLAUDE.md or rules files, typically set in .claude/settings.local.json.

AGENTS.md: read only when no CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, or CLAUDE.local.md exists in cwd or above (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, managed CLAUDE.md and rules still load alongside). Reads AGENTS.md and .claude/AGENTS.md up the tree, plus subdirectory AGENTS.md lazily. Not read: AGENTS.local.md, AGENTS.override.md, .agents/. /config 'Project instructions' setting values: claude-md-or-agents-md (default), claude-md-and-agents-md, and others. Alternative: CLAUDE.md containing '@AGENTS.md'.
Block-level HTML comments are stripped before injection. Max loaded CLAUDE.md size 4 MiB; docs recommend under 200 lines per file.

--add-dir directories do not load their CLAUDE.md unless CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1. --bare disables CLAUDE.md auto-discovery. Project rules are skipped when 'project' is excluded from --setting-sources.

/init generates a CLAUDE.md (CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1 enables an interactive multi-phase flow). /memory lists and opens memory files; /context shows which loaded. /doctor prompt-audit (v2.1.283+) audits instruction files.
InstructionsLoaded hook fires when a CLAUDE.md or rules file loads, with matcher values session_start, nested_traversal, path_glob_match, include, compact.

records.summary: Custom slash commands are Markdown prompt files in .claude/commands/. They have been merged into skills: a file at .claude/commands/deploy.md and a skill at .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md both create /deploy and behave the same. Command files accept the same frontmatter as SKILL.md except 'name' and 'paths'. Subdirectories namespace with ':' and plugin commands are prefixed with the plugin name.
details: Command name: file name without extension; a subdirectory adds a colon-separated segment: .claude/commands/frontend/component.md -> /frontend:component. Plugin: commands/db/migrate.md in my-plugin -> /my-plugin:db:migrate.

Frontmatter supported (same as skills minus name/paths): description, when_to_use, argument-hint, arguments, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, allowed-tools, disallowed-tools, model, effort, context (fork), agent, background, hooks, shell, metadata.

Argument substitution: $ARGUMENTS (all args; appended as 'ARGUMENTS: <value>' if no placeholder), $ARGUMENTS[N] and $N (0-based, shell-style quoting), $name for 'arguments:' declared names, ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}, ${CLAUDE_EFFORT}, ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}, ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} (last two in plugins only). Escape a literal with backslash: \$1.
Dynamic context injection: a line !`cmd` (or a ```! fenced block) runs the shell command and inlines its output before Claude sees the prompt; 'shell: powershell' switches interpreter.

Relation to skills: skills add a directory for supporting files, invocation control, auto-loading by description, and live change detection. Docs recommend skills for new work; .claude/commands/ files keep working. --add-dir directories' .claude/commands/ load but are not watched.

A command is recognized only at the start of a message; up to six skills can be chained (/a /b text). Built-in commands (e.g. /compact, /model) are separate from custom commands; bundled skills (e.g. /debug, /code-review) are prompt-based and listed as 'Skill' in the commands reference.
MCP servers can expose prompts that appear as commands (expansion_type mcp_prompt in UserPromptExpansion hooks).
Permission control: Skill(name) / Skill(name *) rules; a bare 'Skill' deny disables all model-invoked skills. --disable-slash-commands disables all skills.
UserPromptExpansion hook fires when a typed command expands, with command_name, command_args, command_source, expansion_type (slash_command | mcp_prompt); can block.

records.summary: A skill is a directory with SKILL.md (frontmatter + Markdown instructions) and optional supporting files. Descriptions of all skills are always in context; the body loads when the user types /name or when Claude invokes it through the Skill tool. Frontmatter controls who may invoke it, tool pre-approval, model/effort overrides, forked-subagent execution, path scoping, and hooks. Claude Code follows the agentskills.io standard with extensions.
details: Discovery: enterprise (managed dir), personal ~/.claude/skills, project .claude/skills (walked up to repo root), nested subdir skills (load lazily, qualified as /apps/web:deploy on clash), --add-dir dirs, plugins (as /plugin-name:skill-name), and skills synced from claude.ai (as /anthropic-skills:<name>). Folder names 'synced' and 'anthropic-skills' are reserved.

Frontmatter fields (all optional; description recommended): name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint, arguments, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, allowed-tools, disallowed-tools, model, effort, context, agent, background, hooks, paths, shell, metadata. Unknown fields are ignored silently; booleans accept yes/no/on/off/1/0.

Invocation matrix: default = user and Claude can invoke, description in context. disable-model-invocation: true = only user can invoke, description NOT in context, Claude is blocked if it tries. user-invocable: false = hidden from / menu, only Claude invokes.
description + when_to_use are truncated at 1,536 characters in the listing. 'name' overrides the directory name for the command. Frontmatter is read only when '---' is the first line.

allowed-tools pre-approves tools for the invoking turn only (clears on next user message); disallowed-tools removes tools while active. ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} and ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} are substituted in allowed-tools Bash rules and body.
context: fork runs the skill in a forked subagent (agent: picks subagent type; background: false waits for the result). model: applies for the turn; effort: low|medium|high|xhigh|max.
paths: glob list limits auto-activation to when Claude works on matching files (same syntax as rules).
hooks: in frontmatter register when the skill is invoked and persist for the rest of the session; 'once: true' removes a hook after first successful run (skill frontmatter only).

Settings override: skillOverrides map in settings with values on | name-only | user-invocable-only | off (does not affect plugin skills). disableBundledSkills turns off bundled skills. Permission rules: Skill(name), Skill(name *), Skill(skill:name), bare Skill deny.
Skills are watched live in ~/.claude/skills and .claude/skills. A skill folder containing .claude-plugin/plugin.json loads as a plugin named <name>@skills-dir.
Subagents can preload full skill content via the 'skills' frontmatter field. A skill named verify or simplify in a user/project location is run before commits (v2.1.286+).
Bundled skills include /doctor, /code-review, /batch, /debug, /loop, /claude-api, /verify, /run, /simplify, /fewer-permission-prompts, /init, /security-review.

records.nativeName: Hooks (hook events, matcher groups, hook handlers)
records.summary: Hooks are shell commands, HTTP endpoints, MCP tool calls, prompts, or subagents that run at lifecycle events. Configuration is hooks.<Event>[] -> {matcher, hooks: [handler...]}. Command hooks receive JSON on stdin and answer with exit codes (0 success, 2 block, other non-blocking) or a JSON object on stdout. All matching hooks run in parallel; defaults are 600 s timeout for command/http/mcp_tool, 30 s prompt, 60 s agent.
details: Events (34): SessionStart, Setup, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Notification, MessageDisplay, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, Stop, StopFailure, TeammateIdle, InstructionsLoaded, ConfigChange, CwdChanged, DirectoryAdded, FileChanged, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, PreCompact, PostCompact, PreModelSwitch, PostModelSwitch, Elicitation, ElicitationResult, SessionEnd.

Schema: {"hooks": {"<Event>": [{"matcher": "...", "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "...", ...}]}]}}. Plugin hooks/hooks.json uses the same shape plus an optional top-level 'description' and a 'modules' key for mods.

Matcher evaluation: '*', '' or omitted = all; only letters/digits/_/-/space/,/| = exact string or list separated by | or ,; any other char = unanchored JavaScript regex (wrap in ^...$ for whole-string). What it matches per event: tool name (PreToolUse etc.), startup|resume|clear|compact|fork (SessionStart), init|maintenance (Setup), notification type (Notification), agent type (SubagentStart/Stop), manual|auto (Pre/PostCompact), model name (Pre/PostModelSwitch), user_settings|project_settings|local_settings|policy_settings|skills (ConfigChange), filenames (FileChanged), error type (StopFailure), load reason (InstructionsLoaded), command name (UserPromptExpansion).

Handler types: command, http, mcp_tool, prompt, agent. Common fields: type, if (one permission rule e.g. Bash(git *), only on tool events), timeout (seconds), statusMessage, once. Command fields: command, args (exec form, no shell), async, asyncRewake, shell (bash|powershell), onFailure (continue|block, v2.1.295+). HTTP fields: url, headers, allowedEnvVars, onFailure.

Timeouts: default 600 s for command/http/mcp_tool, 30 s for prompt, 60 s for agent; lowered to 30 s on UserPromptSubmit/PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch and 10 s on MessageDisplay; SessionEnd hooks share a 1.5 s budget (raised up to 60 s by explicit timeout). Timed-out hooks are cancelled and their output discarded (no decision).

Input: JSON on stdin (command) or POST body (http). Common fields include session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name, permission_mode, plus agent_id/agent_type inside subagents; tool events add tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id; PostToolUse adds tool_response.

Exit codes: 0 = success (stdout parsed as JSON if a single object, else plain text; only UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, SessionStart, PostModelSwitch add plain stdout as context); 2 = blocking error, stderr shown to Claude as the reason; any other code = non-blocking error, transcript shows '<hook> hook error'. Exit 1 does NOT block unless onFailure: block.

JSON output universal fields: continue (false stops Claude entirely), stopReason, systemMessage, suppressOutput (no effect), terminalSequence. Top-level decision: "block" + reason for UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Stop, SubagentStop, ConfigChange, PreCompact. hookSpecificOutput {hookEventName, ...}: PreToolUse permissionDecision allow|deny|ask|defer + permissionDecisionReason + updatedInput + additionalContext; PermissionRequest decision.behavior allow|deny + updatedInput + permission update entries; PermissionDenied retry; PostToolUse updatedToolOutput; SessionStart/SubagentStart/PostModelSwitch additionalContext (SessionStart also initialUserMessage, watchPaths, sessionTitle, reloadSkills); MessageDisplay displayContent; Elicitation action accept|decline|cancel + content; WorktreeCreate worktreePath (http) or stdout path.
additionalContext, systemMessage, initialUserMessage and plain stdout are capped at 10,000 characters (overflow saved to a file).

Blocking vs advisory: PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, Stop, SubagentStop, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle, PreModelSwitch, PermissionRequest can block or decide; Setup, Notification, SessionEnd, PostCompact, InstructionsLoaded, StopFailure, CwdChanged, DirectoryAdded, FileChanged have no decision control (side effects only). Silence (exit 0, no JSON) never approves; it leaves the normal permission flow.
Async: 'async: true' runs in background without blocking; 'asyncRewake: true' wakes Claude with stderr as a system reminder on exit 2 (used by security-guidance plugin).

Scope and dedupe: same handler in multiple settings files runs once; plugin/skill copies stay separate. Hooks also fire inside subagents. allowManagedHooksOnly (managed) restricts to managed hooks; disableAllHooks exists. Project settings hooks and project subagent frontmatter hooks require workspace trust. --bare skips settings and plugin hooks.

Path placeholders ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} are substituted and exported as env vars; plugin hooks also get CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY> and ${user_config.*} (exec form only). CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true in cloud sessions.
/hooks menu views configured hooks; --include-hook-events emits hook lifecycle events in stream-json output.

records.summary: A plugin is a directory with an optional .claude-plugin/plugin.json manifest and components at the plugin root: skills/, commands/, agents/, hooks/hooks.json, .mcp.json, .lsp.json, output-styles/, workflows/, themes/, monitors/, bin/, settings.json. Plugins are distributed through marketplaces defined by .claude-plugin/marketplace.json and installed with 'claude plugin install <name>@<marketplace>' at user (default), project, or local scope. Enablement is the enabledPlugins map in settings; marketplaces are registered in extraKnownMarketplaces.
details: plugin.json fields (all optional, manifest itself optional): name, displayName, version, description, author {name,email,url}, homepage, repository, license, keywords, defaultEnabled, dependencies, metadata, skills (paths), commands (paths or inline {source|content, description}), agents (paths), hooks (path or inline), mcpServers (inline map, path, or array), lspServers, outputStyles, experimental {themes, monitors}, userConfig {key: {type,title,description,sensitive}}, channels. Unknown top-level keys are stripped.

Standard layout: .claude-plugin/plugin.json; skills/<name>/SKILL.md; commands/*.md; agents/*.md (subfolders become part of the agent name my-plugin:review:security); hooks/hooks.json; .mcp.json; .lsp.json; output-styles/; workflows/*.js; themes/*.json; monitors/monitors.json; bin/ (added to Bash PATH); settings.json (agent and subagentStatusLine defaults). A single SKILL.md at the plugin root loads as a one-skill plugin.

Namespacing: skills and commands become /<plugin>:<name>; agents become <plugin>:<agent>; MCP tools become mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>. Plugin subagents ignore hooks, mcpServers, permissionMode frontmatter.

marketplace.json top-level: name (required; many reserved names), owner {name required, email, url} (required), plugins [] (required), $schema, description, version, metadata.{description,version,pluginRoot}, forceRemoveDeletedPlugins, allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn, renames. Plugin entries: name and source required (source: relative path string, or object {source: github|git|git-subdir|url|npm|..., repo|url, path, ref, sha}), plus category, author, description, homepage, version and any plugin.json field.

Install lifecycle: 'claude plugin marketplace add <owner/repo | git-url | ./path | https://.../marketplace.json>' registers a marketplace (claude-plugins-official is auto-added on first interactive session) -> 'claude plugin install <name>@<marketplace> [--scope user|project|local] [--marketplace <source>]' clones to ~/.claude/plugins/cache and records installed_plugins.json -> enabledPlugins entry written to the scope's settings file -> 'claude plugin enable|disable|uninstall|update <id>' and 'claude plugin marketplace list|update|remove'. /plugin in a session opens the panel (Discover, Installed, Marketplaces, Stats tabs). 'claude plugin validate <path>' checks manifests. --plugin-dir <path> and --plugin-url <zip> load a plugin for one session.

enabledPlugins: map of "<name>@<marketplace>": true|false. Sources merge key by key from lowest to highest: --add-dir settings, user (~/.claude/settings.json), project (.claude/settings.json), local (.claude/settings.local.json), --settings flag, managed (true force-enables, false blocks). Project-scope entries enable for collaborators but each must still run claude plugin install --scope project.

extraKnownMarketplaces: map of "<marketplace-name>": {"source": {"source": "github", "repo": "org/repo"} | {"source":"git","url":...} | {"source":"url"|"file"|"directory",...}, "autoUpdate": bool}. Related managed keys: strictKnownMarketplaces (allowlist), blockedMarketplaces (incl. {"source":"skills-dir"}), strictPluginOnlyCustomization, disableSideloadFlags.

~/.claude/plugins/ layout: installed_plugins.json {version, plugins: {"<id>": [{scope, installPath, version, installedAt, lastUpdated, gitCommitSha}]}}; known_marketplaces.json {"<name>": {source, installLocation, lastUpdated, autoUpdate}}; cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/; marketplaces/<name>/ clones; data/<plugin-id>/ persistent dir exposed as ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} (id with non [A-Za-z0-9_-] replaced by '-').
defaultEnabled: false ships a plugin installed but off until 'claude plugin enable'. Plugins synced from a claude.ai account appear as <name>@synced; organization-required plugins cannot be disabled.

Updates: 'claude plugin update <id>'; marketplace auto-update toggle per marketplace; 'claude plugin marketplace update' with no name refreshes listings only. Plugins load from installed_plugins.json and cache without network at session start.
Plugin evals: 'claude plugin eval' and /skill-doctor report exist (plugin-evals page).

records.format: Markdown with YAML frontmatter (body = system prompt)
records.summary: Subagents are Markdown files whose frontmatter configures name, description, tools, model, permissionMode and more, and whose body is the system prompt. Priority when names collide: managed > --agents CLI > .claude/agents (project, closest dir wins) > ~/.claude/agents (user) > plugin agents/. Claude delegates automatically based on description; users force one with @agent-name or run a whole session as one with --agent.
details: Required frontmatter: name (<=256 chars, no ':'), description. Optional: tools, disallowedTools, model (sonnet|opus|haiku|fable|full id|inherit), permissionMode (default|acceptEdits|auto|dontAsk|bypassPermissions|plan|manual), maxTurns, autoCompactWindow (100000-1000000), skills (preloaded full content), mcpServers (names or inline configs), hooks, memory (user|project|local), background, omitClaudeMd, effort (low|medium|high|xhigh|max), isolation (worktree), color (red|blue|green|yellow|purple|orange|pink|cyan), initialPrompt, experimental {cacheTtl: 5m|1h}. Unknown fields ignored silently; camelCase required.

Scope priority: 1 managed settings dir .claude/agents/, 2 --agents JSON, 3 .claude/agents/ (walk up to repo root; closest to cwd wins), 4 ~/.claude/agents/, 5 plugin agents/. Directories are scanned recursively; subfolders do not affect identity except in plugins where they become part of the id (my-plugin:review:security).
--agents accepts a JSON object {name: {description, prompt, tools, model, ...}}; with -p it also accepts a file path (v2.1.281+). color and experimental are ignored there.
Plugin subagents ignore hooks, mcpServers, and permissionMode frontmatter for security.

Invocation: automatic delegation from description; natural language; @-mention via typeahead or typed @agent-<name> / @agent-<plugin>:<name>; session-wide with --agent <name> or the 'agent' setting. Agent(AgentName) permission rules allow/deny specific subagents; Agent(model:opus) and Agent(isolation:worktree) parameter rules exist.

records.summary: MCP servers are added with 'claude mcp add' (default scope local) or by editing .mcp.json / ~/.claude.json. Three user scopes: local (this project, private, stored in ~/.claude.json under the project path), project (.mcp.json committed to the repo, requires per-user approval), user (all projects, ~/.claude.json). Transports: stdio, http (alias streamable-http), sse, ws; OAuth 2.0 is supported for http/sse via /mcp or 'claude mcp login'. Admins deploy a fixed set with managed-mcp.json or provide servers with managedMcpServers and filter with allowedMcpServers/deniedMcpServers.
details: CLI: claude mcp add [--transport stdio|http|sse] [--scope local|project|user] [--env KEY=val] [--header 'Name: val'] <name> [url | -- command args]; claude mcp add-json <name> '<json>'; claude mcp list|get <name>|remove <name> [--scope]; claude mcp login <name>; claude mcp reset-project-choices. OAuth 2.0: for http (and sse) servers; dynamic client registration or CIMD by default; pre-configured credentials via --client-id, --client-secret (prompted), --callback-port or an oauth object in add-json; tokens stored per endpoint, deleted on remove. 401 triggers one refresh+retry. -p runs cannot run the flow; sign in first interactively or with claude mcp login.

records.summary: Permission rules have the form Tool or Tool(specifier) and live in permissions.allow / ask / deny arrays; evaluation order is deny, then ask, then allow, first match wins, and a deny at any scope cannot be overridden anywhere. permissions.defaultMode picks the starting mode: default (Manual), acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions. The sandbox (sandbox.enabled) is an OS-level boundary (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap+socat on Linux/WSL2) around Bash commands with filesystem and network allow/deny lists.
details: Rule syntax: bare tool name (Bash, Read, WebFetch, Skill) matches all uses and as a deny removes the tool from context; Bash(*) == Bash. Bash(npm run *): '*' matches any text; trailing ' *' also matches the bare command; 'Bash(ls:*)' is the equivalent suffix form; wildcard before the subcommand (Bash(git * main)) warns. Compound commands split on && || ; | |& & and newlines; each subcommand must match; wrappers timeout/time/nice/nohup/stdbuf/command/builtin/noglob/xargs are stripped.

Read(path)/Edit(path): gitignore syntax; //abs for filesystem root, ~/ for home, /path relative to the settings source (project dir for project/local), path or ./path relative to cwd. Read deny also blocks Edit/Write on the path and recognized Bash file commands/redirections. Write/NotebookEdit/Glob path rules are accepted but never consulted (use Edit/Read).

WebFetch(domain:example.com), WebFetch(domain:*.example.com), WebFetch(domain:*) (also feeds the sandbox domain list; bare WebFetch does not). MCP: mcp__server, mcp__server__tool, mcp__server__* (allow globs only after a literal mcp__<server>__ prefix; deny may use '*' or 'mcp__*'). Agent(Name), Skill(name), Skill(name *), Cd(path). Parameter rules for deny/ask: Tool(param:value) e.g. Agent(model:opus), Bash(run_in_background:true), Bash(dangerouslyDisableSandbox:true); not for primary content fields (command, file_path, url).

Evaluation: deny -> ask -> allow, first match wins regardless of specificity; deny from any scope beats allow from any scope, including --allowedTools; --disallowedTools adds restrictions. Project .claude/settings.json allow rules and additionalDirectories apply only after the workspace trust dialog.

Modes (permissions.defaultMode / --permission-mode): default (alias manual, prompts on first use), acceptEdits (auto-accepts edits and mkdir/touch/mv/cp in working dirs), plan (read-only exploration, edits blocked until plan approved), auto (background classifier reviews shell commands and network actions; session-level rules in autoMode: environment/allow/soft_deny/hard_deny with "$defaults"; autoMode.classifyAllShell routes every shell command through it), dontAsk (auto-deny anything that would prompt), bypassPermissions (skip prompts; --dangerously-skip-permissions). auto and bypassPermissions do not take effect from project or local settings (v2.1.257+). Shift+Tab cycles modes in the TUI.

Locks: permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable" and permissions.disableAutoMode (or top-level disableAutoMode) "disable"; allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly ignores non-managed allow rules; permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories; permissions.additionalDirectories persists --add-dir. Protected paths (.git, .claude, etc.) and critical-path rm still prompt in most modes.

'Yes, and don't ask again' saves an allow rule to .claude/settings.local.json at the repo root (Bash prefix, WebFetch domain); file-edit approvals last only for the session. /permissions dialog edits rules live. --allowedTools/--disallowedTools use the same syntax.

Sandbox: off by default; enable with /sandbox (writes .claude/settings.local.json) or sandbox.enabled: true. Keys: sandbox.enabled, failIfUnavailable, autoAllowBashIfSandboxed (auto-allow mode), excludedCommands, allowUnsandboxedCommands (false = strict mode), filesystem.{allowWrite, denyWrite, denyRead, allowRead, allowManagedReadPathsOnly, disabled}, network.{allowedDomains, deniedDomains, allowUnixSockets, allowAllUnixSockets, allowLocalBinding, allowMachLookup, strictAllowlist, allowManagedDomainsOnly, httpProxyPort, socksProxyPort, tlsTerminate}, credentials.{files, envVars, allowPlaintextInject, awsPairs, sigv4}, ignoreViolations, enableWeakerNestedSandbox, enableWeakerNetworkIsolation, allowAppleEvents, ripgrep, bwrapPath, socatPath.

Sandbox defaults: writes allowed to cwd, per-user $TMPDIR, and added directories; reads mostly open (deny with denyRead/credentials); network goes through a local proxy with an empty allowlist that prompts per new domain (auto mode: per-command allowed domains for the classifier). Sandbox covers Bash/PowerShell/Monitor only; Read/Edit/WebFetch tools, hooks, MCP servers, LSP run outside it. Claude can retry a failed command with dangerouslyDisableSandbox unless allowUnsandboxedCommands is false. Built on @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime; native Windows runs unsandboxed.
Sandbox filesystem arrays merge across scopes; a managed false for allowUnsandboxedCommands makes the sandbox admin-required and ignores loosening repository settings.

records.summary: Two memory systems load every session: CLAUDE.md files (written by you) and auto memory (written by Claude). Auto memory lives in ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ with a MEMORY.md index (first 200 lines or 25 KB loaded) and one topic file per memory, keyed by git repo so worktrees share it. Session transcripts are JSONL under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/ and are resumed with --continue, --resume <id|name|path>, or /resume; retention is cleanupPeriodDays (30 days default).
details: Auto memory: on by default locally; toggle in /memory (writes autoMemoryEnabled to ~/.claude/settings.json), per-project autoMemoryEnabled: false, or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1. Off by default in self-hosted environments; cannot be re-enabled from background or nested sessions.

Memory file types recorded in frontmatter 'type': user, feedback, project, reference. Claude Code adds a 'modified' ISO timestamp to frontmatter on write (v2.1.214+). Claude skips facts derivable from code or already in CLAUDE.md.

Location: ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ where <project> derives from the git repo root (shared across worktrees); override with autoMemoryDirectory (absolute or ~/ path, any scope) or CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Excluded from the retention sweep.

Loading: MEMORY.md first 200 lines / 25 KB at session start; topic files read on demand; Claude Code warns or errors when the index exceeds the limit. Not loaded into subagents (except forks); subagents can have their own memory via the 'memory' frontmatter field (user scope -> ~/.claude/agent-memory/<name>/).

Transcripts: ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl (<project> = cwd path with non-alphanumerics replaced by '-', truncated at 200 chars + hash). Format is internal; use /export or 'claude -p --resume <id> --output-format json' for scripting. ~/.claude/history.jsonl holds typed prompts for up-arrow and Ctrl+R.

Resume: claude --continue (most recent in cwd), claude --resume [<session-id>|<name>|<transcript-path>] (picker with no arg), --fork-session, --session-id <uuid>, --from-pr, /resume, /rename, /branch, /clear, --name. -p and SDK sessions are hidden from the picker and --continue but resumable by id; -p --continue includes them. --no-session-persistence disables saving in -p.

Resumed sessions restore the model they used and, from a terminal, the permission mode (plan mode handling has special rules). Retention: cleanupPeriodDays (default 30) and desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays; 'claude purge' deletes a project's state.
Checkpointing/rewind (/rewind) is separate; CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY suppresses transcript writes; CLAUDE_CODE_TRANSCRIPT_LOCAL_GC limits -p transcript growth.
CLAUDE.md as memory: /memory lists CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and auto memory locations; asking Claude to 'remember' saves to auto memory, asking to 'add this to CLAUDE.md' edits the file.

A bare Bash entry in --allowedTools is dropped in auto mode. Workspace trust dialog is skipped in -p; invalid settings files are silently ignored.

Output: json result includes result, session_id, total_cost_usd, per-model usage (modelUsage), permission_denials, mcp_servers, mcp_server_errors (array of {name,type,message} when --mcp-config entries are skipped). stream-json emits newline-delimited events (system/init, assistant, user, result; permission_denied system messages; hook_started/hook_progress/hook_response with --include-hook-events).

Multi-turn: --continue (most recent conversation; includes -p sessions), --resume <session-id|transcript path>, --fork-session. -p sessions are hidden from the interactive picker. SIGTERM exits 143 without finishing the turn; SIGINT ends the turn. Background work at exit waits up to 10 minutes.

Bare mode (--bare, sets CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1): skips hooks, LSP, plugin sync, auto-memory, CLAUDE.md discovery, keychain; auth strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper via --settings; provide context explicitly with --system-prompt, --add-dir, --mcp-config, --settings, --agents, --plugin-dir. --restricted removes code-running tools and ignores user/project/local settings.

The docs call 'claude -p' the CLI form of the Agent SDK.

records.summary: Hooks are stable and on by default (features.hooks = true). They are declared in hooks.json or inline [hooks] TOML at user, project, plugin and managed layers; all matching hooks from every file run, concurrently. Each hook is {type: command|mcp_tool, command, timeout(seconds), statusMessage, async, additionalContextLimit} under a matcher group. Codex reads a JSON event on stdin and accepts JSON on stdout, exit 2 blocks. Non-managed hooks must be trusted via /hooks; trust is a hash stored in config.toml [hooks.state].
details: Enable/disable: [features] hooks = true|false (alias codex_hooks deprecated). Project-local hooks load only when the project is trusted.

Events (12): PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Stop, Interrupt, PreCompact, PostCompact (turn-scoped); SessionStart, SessionEnd (session-scoped).

Shape: {"description"?, "hooks": {"<Event>": [{"matcher": "<regex>", "hooks": [{"type":"command","command":"...","timeout":600,"statusMessage":"...","async":false,"additionalContextLimit":2500}]}]}}. Inline TOML: [[hooks.PreToolUse]] matcher=... / [[hooks.PreToolUse.hooks]] type="command" command=...

Matchers: regex; "*", "" or omitted = match all. Values: tool names for PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PermissionRequest (Bash, apply_patch, mcp__server__tool); manual|auto for PreCompact/PostCompact; startup|resume|clear|compact|fork for SessionStart; subagent type for SubagentStart/Stop; not supported for UserPromptSubmit/Stop/Interrupt.
Timeout in seconds; default 600; SessionEnd/Interrupt default 1 s, max 3 s.
stdin JSON: session_id, hook_event_name, cwd, transcript_path, model, turn_id, permission_mode; PreToolUse adds tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id; PostToolUse adds tool_response.

stdout JSON: continue, stopReason, systemMessage, suppressOutput, hookSpecificOutput{permissionDecision allow|deny, permissionDecisionReason, updatedInput (PreToolUse); additionalContext (UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart)}. Exit 0 = ok; exit 2 + stderr = block (PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse); other non-zero = reported, non-blocking.
type "mcp_tool": server, tool, input (templates ${field.nested}), timeout, statusMessage. Prompt/agent handler types are parsed but skipped.

Trust: new/changed hooks are flagged at startup; /hooks lets you review, trust, or disable; trust stored as [hooks.state."<file>:<event>:<i>:<j>"] trusted_hash in config.toml. --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust skips the check for one run. requirements.toml allow_managed_hooks_only = true ignores user/project/plugin hooks.
Plugin hooks: manifest "hooks": "./hooks/hooks.json" (or default hooks/hooks.json); env PLUGIN_ROOT, PLUGIN_DATA (+ CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA aliases); not auto-trusted on install.
Portability: the shared matcher/command envelope does not guarantee compatibility. Validate supported events, handler/output fields, environment variables and Codex trust before reuse.

records.summary: Two orthogonal knobs: sandbox_mode (read-only | workspace-write | danger-full-access) controls what commands can touch; approval_policy (on-request | never | { granular = {...} }) controls when Codex asks. The 'untrusted' and 'on-failure' values are retired; --full-auto is no longer supported, replaced by --sandbox workspace-write; --yolo aliases --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox. Starlark prefix_rule files in rules/ dirs pre-decide commands (allow|prompt|forbidden). A newer beta permissions-profile system (default_permissions, [permissions.<name>]) is mutually exclusive with sandbox_mode.
details: approval_policy: "on-request" | "never" | { granular = { sandbox_approval, rules, mcp_elicitations, request_permissions, skill_approval } }. `codex --ask-for-approval` accepts only on-request | never in 0.162.1. 'untrusted' retired; 'on-failure' not offered.

Presets: Read-only = --sandbox read-only --ask-for-approval on-request; Auto = --sandbox workspace-write --ask-for-approval on-request; Full access = --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox (alias --yolo). --approve-for-me (alias --not-so-yolo) routes approvals to an automatic reviewer with workspace-write; approvals_reviewer = "user" | "auto_review".
--full-auto: 'no longer supported. Update scripts to use --sandbox workspace-write'.
Enforcement: macOS Seatbelt; Linux/WSL2 bubblewrap (first bwrap on PATH) + seccomp; Windows windows.sandbox = mxc|elevated|unelevated. `codex sandbox -- <cmd>` runs a command under the sandbox.

records.format: MDC (Markdown with YAML frontmatter) for .mdc; plain Markdown for AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules
records.summary: Project Rules are .mdc files in .cursor/rules/ with frontmatter keys description, globs and alwaysApply; the combination of those keys selects one of four rule types. Nested .cursor/rules directories are supported. AGENTS.md (root and nested) and CLAUDE.md are read as plain-Markdown rules. The legacy single .cursorrules file is deprecated but still read. User Rules are account-synced text set in Customize > Rules; Team Rules are dashboard-managed (Team/Enterprise). Order of application: Team Rules, then Project Rules, then User Rules.
details: Frontmatter keys: description (string), globs (comma-separated file patterns), alwaysApply (boolean).

Rule types by frontmatter: Always Apply = alwaysApply: true (globs and description ignored); Apply Intelligently (a.k.a. Agent Requested) = alwaysApply: false + description; Apply to Specific Files (Auto Attached) = alwaysApply: false + globs; Apply Manually = alwaysApply: false with no description/globs, included only when @-mentioned.

Nested rules: 'Cursor rules inside the project can live in nested directories' (built-in migrate-to-skills skill uses pattern {workspaceFolder}/**/.cursor/rules/*.mdc). Help page says rules are identified by full file path and a flat layout is recommended.

AGENTS.md: plain Markdown, no frontmatter, placed at the project root or in subdirectories; nested AGENTS.md instructions are combined hierarchically with the more specific one taking precedence. CLAUDE.md at the project root is also read and 'always applied' for Claude Code compatibility. The CLI docs list .cursor/rules, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md as the rule sources it loads.
Legacy .cursorrules: deprecated; 'Cursor still reads it'; migrate with the 'New Cursor Rule' command.
User Rules: Customize > Rules (IDE), stored in the Cursor account and synced across devices; apply to Agent (Chat) only, not to Inline Edit (Cmd/Ctrl+K), Tab, or Bugbot.
Team Rules: Team/Enterprise plans, managed in the dashboard, support glob patterns, can be marked required or optional. Precedence when rules conflict: Team Rules > Project Rules > User Rules.
Size guidance: keep rules under 500 lines (docs); built-in create-rule skill recommends under 50 lines and one concern per rule.

Bugbot has its own rule file family: .cursor/BUGBOT.md at the repo root plus nested BUGBOT.md files found while traversing upward from changed files; each rule truncated at 30,000 chars, combined cap 100,000 chars; order Team Rules > project BUGBOT.md > learned rules.
Plugins ship rules via the manifest key rules (default dir rules/, accepting .md, .mdc, .markdown).
CLI helper: `agent generate-rule` (alias `rule`) creates a rule interactively.
Migration: 'Apply Intelligently' rules (description, no globs, no alwaysApply: true) are candidates for /migrate-to-skills conversion to .cursor/skills/<name>/SKILL.md.

records.summary: Skills are directories containing SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter (name, description required). The agent chooses skills from their descriptions unless disable-model-invocation: true restricts them to explicit /name invocation. Cursor ships first-party built-ins in ~/.cursor/skills-cursor/ (create-hook, create-rule, create-skill, create-subagent, migrate-to-skills, and others); rules and commands can be converted to skills with /migrate-to-skills.
details: Required frontmatter: name (max 64 chars, lowercase letters/numbers/hyphens, should match folder), description (max 1024 chars, non-empty, third person, include WHAT and WHEN).

Optional frontmatter (docs): paths (globs that scope the skill to matching files; legacy globs still accepted), disable-model-invocation (true = only via /skill-name), icon, color (Custom Mode badge), metadata (arbitrary key-values). Built-ins also use environments / disabled-environments (values seen: local, cloud) and metadata.surfaces (values seen: cli, ide, cloud).

Discovery: four standard locations (.agents/skills, .cursor/skills, ~/.agents/skills, ~/.cursor/skills) plus compatibility paths .claude/skills, .codex/skills and their home equivalents; nested skill directories are auto-scoped to files inside that directory.

Personal skills in the IDE live in the 'user Agent Store' (synced across machines), not ~/.cursor/skills; the create-skill skill says to fall back to ~/.cursor/skills/<name>/ only when no store is mounted, and never to write into ~/.cursor/skills-cursor/ (reserved, system-managed).
Invocation: automatic by description; manual via / menu in Agent chat and CLI; @skill-name attaches as context; Option+Enter / Alt+Enter keeps a skill active as a Custom Mode.
Body guidance: SKILL.md under 500 lines, progressive disclosure to one-level-deep reference files, scripts in any language.

records.format: JSON {version: 1, hooks: {<event>: [{command|prompt, type, timeout, matcher, failClosed, loop_limit}]}}
records.summary: Hooks are declared in hooks.json with schema version 1 and a hooks map keyed by camelCase event name. Each entry is a command hook (script exchanging JSON over stdin/stdout) or a prompt hook (LLM-judged). Sources merge with precedence Enterprise (MDM) > Team (cloud) > Project > User, and permission results merge so deny beats ask beats allow. Exit code 2 blocks; other non-zero exits fail open unless failClosed: true.
details: Shape: {"version": 1, "hooks": {"afterFileEdit": [{"command": ".cursor/hooks/format.sh"}]}}. Entry fields: command, type ("command" default | "prompt"), prompt (for prompt hooks, may include $ARGUMENTS), timeout (seconds, default platform-dependent), matcher (JavaScript regex; "" or "*" matches all), failClosed (default false), loop_limit (default 5; for stop/subagentStop follow-up loops).

Agent events: sessionStart, sessionEnd, preToolUse, postToolUse, postToolUseFailure, subagentStart, subagentStop, beforeShellExecution, afterShellExecution, beforeMCPExecution, afterMCPExecution, beforeReadFile, afterFileEdit, beforeSubmitPrompt, preCompact, stop, afterAgentResponse, afterAgentThought. Tab events: beforeTabFileRead, afterTabFileEdit. App lifecycle: workspaceOpen (runs in desktop app and CLI).

Matcher targets: preToolUse/postToolUse/postToolUseFailure match tool type (Shell, Read, Write, Grep, Delete, Task, MCP:<tool_name>); subagentStart/Stop match subagent type (generalPurpose, explore, shell); before/afterShellExecution match the command string; beforeReadFile = Read; afterFileEdit = Write; beforeTabFileRead = TabRead; afterTabFileEdit = TabWrite; beforeSubmitPrompt = UserPromptSubmit; stop = Stop; afterAgentResponse = AgentResponse; afterAgentThought = AgentThought.

Common stdin fields: conversation_id, generation_id, model, model_id, model_params[], hook_event_name, cursor_version, workspace_roots[], user_email, transcript_path. Event-specific stdin: beforeShellExecution {command, cwd, sandbox}; afterFileEdit {file_path, edits[{old_string,new_string}]}; beforeReadFile {file_path, content, attachments}; beforeSubmitPrompt {prompt, attachments}; stop {status, loop_count}; sessionStart {is_background_agent, composer_mode}; preToolUse {tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id, cwd}; postToolUse {tool_output, duration}; subagentStart {subagent_id, subagent_type, task, parent_conversation_id, tool_call_id, subagent_model, is_parallel_worker}; subagentStop {subagent_type, status, task, summary, duration_ms, loop_count, modified_files}; workspaceOpen {workspace_roots, user_email}.

Stdout contract: permission hooks (beforeShellExecution, beforeMCPExecution, beforeReadFile, beforeTabFileRead, subagentStart, preToolUse) return {permission: allow|deny|ask, user_message?, agent_message?}; preToolUse may add updated_input; observational hooks (postToolUse, afterShellExecution, afterFileEdit) return {additional_context?, updated_mcp_tool_output?}; sessionStart returns {env?, additional_context?}; stop/subagentStop return {followup_message?}; beforeSubmitPrompt returns {continue: bool, user_message?}; workspaceOpen returns {pluginPaths}. Prompt hooks yield {ok: boolean, reason?}.
Exit codes: 0 success (use JSON), 2 block (same as deny), other non-zero fail open unless failClosed: true.

Env vars available to hook processes: CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR, CURSOR_VERSION, CURSOR_USER_EMAIL, CURSOR_TRANSCRIPT_PATH, CURSOR_CODE_REMOTE, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (alias). Plugin hooks get CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT (superpowers session-start script branches on it; Cursor may also set CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT). sessionStart env output is passed to later hooks in the session.

Path resolution: project hooks run from the project root (.cursor/hooks/x.sh); user hooks run from ~/.cursor/ (./hooks/x.sh). Cursor watches hooks.json and reloads on save; debug via the Hooks tab in Customize or the Hooks output channel.

Cloud agents run command-based hooks from the repo's .cursor/hooks.json only (no ~/.cursor/hooks.json); Enterprise cloud agents also run team and MDM hooks. Hooks do not run during early read-only exploratory turns in cloud.

Plugin hooks: manifest key hooks (path or inline); plugin hooks.json omits or includes version and uses the same camelCase events; the superpowers plugin ships hooks-cursor.json (sessionStart) separately from its Claude Code hooks.json (SessionStart with nested hooks[] and matcher).

records.summary: OpenCode reads a single schema of settings from several JSON/JSONC files and deep-merges them; later sources override earlier ones, and array values such as instructions and plugin are concatenated/deduplicated rather than replaced. Every file should declare "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json"; the global file is auto-created with only that key. Values support {env:VAR} and {file:path} substitution. Config is loaded once at startup and is not hot-reloaded; unknown top-level keys fail startup with ConfigInvalidError.
details: Merge order as implemented in packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts (v1.18.35), lowest to highest: (1) remote .well-known/opencode config for authenticated providers, (2) global ~/.config/opencode/{config.json,opencode.json,opencode.jsonc}, (3) $OPENCODE_CONFIG file, (4) project opencode.jsonc/opencode.json files found walking up from cwd to worktree (outermost first, innermost last), (5) every discovered .opencode directory's opencode.json/opencode.jsonc plus its agent/command/plugin markdown and files, in order: global config dir, project .opencode dirs, ~/.opencode, $OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR, (6) $OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, (7) system managed dir opencode.json/jsonc, (8) macOS MDM plist ai.opencode.managed (overrides everything).
Objects are merged with remeda mergeDeep; `instructions` arrays are unioned; `plugin` arrays are concatenated and de-duplicated by package name or file URL (last declaration wins).
$schema URL: https://opencode.ai/config.json. The TUI has a separate file tui.json with schema https://opencode.ai/tui.json ($OPENCODE_TUI_CONFIG overrides its path).

Variable substitution regexes: /\{env:([^}]+)\}/g replaced from process.env (missing var becomes empty string); /\{file:[^}]+\}/g replaced with file contents, path relative to the config file's directory, `~/` expands to home, missing file is a hard InvalidError. Tokens on lines starting with // are left alone. Shell-style ${VAR} is NOT substituted.

Env flags affecting loading: OPENCODE_CONFIG, OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR, OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1 (skip project files and .opencode dirs; escape hatch for a broken project config), OPENCODE_PERMISSION (JSON merged into permission), OPENCODE_PURE / --pure (skip external plugins), OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS.

Templates support $ARGUMENTS, positional $1..$N, shell injection with !`cmd`, and @path file inclusion. A command file named test.md is invoked as /test and can shadow a built-in.
details: Schema Config.CommandEncoded: template (required), description, agent, model (provider/model or {providerID, model, variant}), subagent (boolean), subtask ("Deprecated alias for subagent"). The 1.18.35 built-in skill lists optional fields: description, agent, model, variant, subtask.
Markdown form: frontmatter keys become config fields; the body (trimmed) becomes `template`. Do not put `template:` in frontmatter.

Placeholders: $ARGUMENTS = everything typed after the command; $1, $2, ... = positional args; !`command` = run shell and inject stdout (regex /!`([^`]+)`/g in config/markdown.ts); @filename = inline file contents (regex /(?<![\w`])@(\.?[^\s`,.]*(?:\.[^\s`,.]+)*)/g).
`subtask: true` forces the command to run in a subagent session.

Built-in commands listed in docs/TUI: /init, /undo, /redo, /share, /unshare, /help, /compact (/summarize), /connect, /details, /editor, /exit (/quit,/q), /export, /models, /new (/clear), /sessions (/resume,/continue), /themes, /thinking. Custom commands with matching names override built-ins.
Headless: `opencode run --command <name> [args...]` runs a command non-interactively, using the message as arguments.
Skills can also be exposed as slash commands via SKILL.md metadata `opencode/slash: "true"` (see skills).
Invalid frontmatter in a command file throws InvalidError and aborts config load (agents fail softly, commands do not).

records.summary: Skills are folders containing SKILL.md with name and description frontmatter. OpenCode discovers them in .opencode/skill(s), the Claude Code and agents.md compatibility locations, and any `skills.paths`/`skills.urls` from config. The model loads them on demand through the built-in `skill` tool; access is gated by the `permission.skill` ruleset, and the whole tool can be disabled per agent. OpenCode also ships a built-in skill, customize-opencode, about its own configuration.
details: Frontmatter: name (required, 1-64 chars, ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$, must match folder name), description (required in practice; 1-1024 chars; skills without one are filtered out), optional license, compatibility, metadata (string map).
Recognised metadata keys: `opencode/slash: "true"` exposes the skill as a /name command; `opencode/autoinvoke: "false"` hides it from the model-facing list (still loadable explicitly).

Discovery order per docs: project .opencode/skills, .claude/skills, .agents/skills (walking up to the git worktree); then global ~/.config/opencode/skills, ~/.claude/skills, ~/.agents/skills. Loader glob in core/skill.ts: {*.md,**/SKILL.md}.
Invocation: model calls skill({ name: "skill-name" }); the tool description lists available skills.

Permissions: `permission.skill` accepts allow|ask|deny or a {pattern: action} object, e.g. {"*": "allow", "internal-*": "deny"}; agents can override in frontmatter `permission.skill`; `tools: { skill: false }` on an agent removes the tool entirely.

`skills` config key: array of paths/URLs, or object {paths: [...], urls: [...]} (object form marked deprecated in the live schema). URLs must serve index.json {skills:[{name, version?, files:[...]}]}; files are downloaded into ~/.cache/opencode/skills/<hash>/<name>/.
Env: OPENCODE_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS=1 skips ~/.claude and ~/.agents scans; OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS=1 skips ~/.claude/skills only.
Plugins can register skill folders at runtime by mutating `config.skills.paths` in their `config` hook (pattern used by the superpowers plugin).
`opencode debug skill` lists all discovered skills with name, description, location and content.

records.summary: OpenCode has no shell-hook config file. Lifecycle interception is done by plugins that return a Hooks object whose keys are event names; each hook receives (input, output) and mutates output in place. The `event` hook receives every bus event (session.*, message.*, file.edited, permission.asked, etc.). An older `experimental.hook` config with `file_edited` and `session_completed` shell commands exists in SDK 1.4.10 types but is not in the 1.18.35 schema or source.
details: Hooks interface keys at v1.18.35 (packages/plugin/src/index.ts; identical set in installed @opencode-ai/plugin 1.4.10 except `dispose`): event, config, tool (object map of custom tools), auth (object), provider (object), dispose, "chat.message", "chat.params", "chat.headers", "permission.ask", "command.execute.before", "tool.execute.before", "shell.env", "tool.execute.after", "tool.definition", "experimental.chat.messages.transform", "experimental.chat.system.transform", "experimental.session.compacting", "experimental.compaction.autocontinue", "experimental.text.complete".

Signatures: tool.execute.before(input:{tool, sessionID, callID}, output:{args}); tool.execute.after(input:{tool, sessionID, callID, args}, output:{title, output, metadata}); permission.ask(input: Permission, output:{status: "ask"|"deny"|"allow"}); chat.message(input:{sessionID, agent?, model?, messageID?, variant?}, output:{message: UserMessage, parts: Part[]}); chat.params(input:{sessionID, agent, model, provider, message}, output:{temperature, topP, topK, maxOutputTokens, options}); chat.headers(..., output:{headers}); shell.env(input:{cwd, sessionID?, callID?}, output:{env}); command.execute.before(input:{command, sessionID, arguments}, output:{parts}); tool.definition(input:{toolID}, output:{description, parameters}); config(config) called once with the merged config (mutable); event({event}) for every bus event.

Experimental hooks: experimental.chat.messages.transform(output.messages[]), experimental.chat.system.transform(output.system: string[]), experimental.session.compacting(output.context[], output.prompt?), experimental.compaction.autocontinue(output.enabled), experimental.text.complete(output.text).

Bus event names documented for the `event` hook: session.created, session.compacted, session.deleted, session.diff, session.error, session.idle, session.status, session.updated, message.part.removed, message.part.updated, message.removed, message.updated, command.executed, file.edited, file.watcher.updated, installation.updated, lsp.client.diagnostics, lsp.updated, permission.asked, permission.replied, server.connected, tui.prompt.append, tui.command.execute, tui.toast.show, shell.env, experimental.session.compacting.

A plugin's `permission.ask` hook can auto-allow or auto-deny permission prompts; `tool.execute.before` can rewrite or block tool args by throwing.
Hooks run inside the opencode server process (Bun). `--pure` / OPENCODE_PURE=1 disables all external plugins and thus all hooks.

records.summary: A plugin is an ES module exporting an async function (input, options?) => Promise<Hooks>. Plugins are declared as npm specs, local paths, file URLs or [spec, options] tuples in the `plugin` array, or auto-discovered from .opencode/plugin(s). npm plugins are installed with Bun at startup. Custom tools are built with the `tool()` helper from @opencode-ai/plugin either inside a plugin's `tool` map or as standalone files under .opencode/tool(s).
details: `plugin` entries: "pkg" (latest), "pkg@1.2.3" (pinned), "pkg@git+https://...#tag" (git spec), "./local-plugin.ts" (relative to the declaring config file), "file:///abs/plugin.js", or ["pkg", {options}] tuple. v2 schema also allows {package, options} objects.

PluginInput fields (v1.18.35): client (createOpencodeClient instance bound to the running server), project, directory, worktree, serverUrl (URL), $ (Bun shell), experimental_workspace.register(type, adapter). Plugin type: (input: PluginInput, options?: PluginOptions) => Promise<Hooks>. PluginModule: {id?, server: Plugin, tui?: never}. Any named export or default export that is a function is loaded.

Custom tools: tool({ description, args: { name: tool.schema.string() ... } (Zod raw shape), async execute(args, context) }) where context = {sessionID, messageID, agent, directory, worktree, abort: AbortSignal, metadata(), ask()}. Return a string or {output, metadata}. tool.schema is Zod. In a plugin, return { tool: { my_tool: tool({...}) } }. As files, the filename becomes the tool name and extra named exports become <file>_<export>; custom tools with built-in names override built-ins.

Dependency handling: OpenCode runs a background `install` of @opencode-ai/plugin (pinned to the running version) into every discovered config directory, creating package.json; local plugins needing other packages list them in that directory's package.json. Plugin failures surface as toast errors, e.g. "Failed to install plugin <pkg>@<version>".

Built-in plugins ship inside the binary (provider plugins for anthropic, openai, github-copilot, opencode, etc.) and are disabled with OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS=1; `--pure`/OPENCODE_PURE=1 skips external plugins only.
CLI: `opencode plugin <module> [-g|--global] [-f|--force]` installs an npm plugin and appends it to the project (or global) opencode.json.
Installed @opencode-ai/plugin 1.4.10 depends on @opencode-ai/sdk 1.4.10, zod 4.1.8 and effect; exports ".", "./tool", "./tui".

Third-party example: obra/superpowers ships .opencode/plugins/superpowers.js exporting `SuperpowersPlugin = async ({ client, directory }) => ({ config, 'experimental.chat.messages.transform' })` and is installed via a git+https plugin spec.

records.summary: Agents are named configurations with mode primary (user drives them, switch with Tab), subagent (invoked by @name or by the task tool) or all. Built-ins: build (default primary, all tools), plan (primary, edit/bash restricted), general and explore (subagents), plus hidden system agents compaction, title, summary. Agents are defined inline under `agent` or as Markdown files whose body is the system prompt; fields include description, mode, model, variant, temperature, top_p, prompt, permission, tools (deprecated), disable, hidden, steps, color.
details: Schema AgentConfig (v1): model, variant, temperature, top_p, prompt, tools {name: boolean} (deprecated, use permission), disable, description, mode (subagent|primary|all), hidden (hide from @ autocomplete; subagents only), options (free-form provider options), color (#RRGGBB or primary|secondary|accent|success|warning|error|info), steps (max agentic iterations), maxSteps (deprecated), permission (PermissionConfig).
v2 schema Config.AgentEncoded: model, request {headers, body}, system, description, mode, hidden, color, steps, disabled, permissions (ordered rule array).

Markdown form: frontmatter = fields, body = prompt; built-in skill says allowed frontmatter keys are name, model, variant, description, mode, hidden, color, steps, options, permission, disable, temperature, top_p and unknown keys are routed into `options`. `prompt` may also be given inline as "{file:./prompts/x.txt}".

Built-in agents per docs: Build (default primary, all tools), Plan (restricted: file edits and bash set to ask/deny), General (subagent for research and multi-step tasks), Explore (fast read-only subagent), Scout (read-only subagent for external docs; docs page only, not in the schema's named list), Compaction/Title/Summary (hidden system agents). Schema named keys: plan, build, general, explore, title, summary, compaction.
Override a built-in by defining the same key under `agent`; disable with `agent: { build: { disable: true } }`. `default_agent` must name a non-hidden primary agent.

Switching: TUI keybind agent_cycle = tab, agent_cycle_reverse = shift+tab (keybinds in tui.json). Subagents invoked with @name in the prompt or by the primary agent via the `task` tool (permission key `task`, patterns match subagent names). `subagent_depth` (v2: experimental.subagent_depth) defaults to 1, preventing subagents from spawning subagents.
Per-agent `permission` merges over global permission with the agent's rules taking precedence; per-agent `tools` can enable/disable MCP tools using glob patterns.

CLI: `opencode agent create` (interactive; flags --path, --description, --mode all|primary|subagent, --permissions), `opencode agent list`, `opencode debug agent <name>`; `opencode run --agent <name>` and `opencode --agent <name>` select the primary agent.
Legacy `mode` config and .opencode/mode(s)/*.md are merged into `agent` with mode forced to primary.

records.summary: MCP servers are configured under `mcp` with a required `type` of local (command array, optional cwd, environment) or remote (url, optional headers, oauth). Each entry supports enabled and timeout (default 5000 ms). Remote servers auto-detect OAuth on 401 and use Dynamic Client Registration unless `oauth: false`. Per-server tools are enabled or disabled through the `tools` config using glob patterns, globally or per agent, and managed with the `opencode mcp` CLI.
details: Local (McpLocalConfig): type "local", command: string[] (required), cwd (relative to workspace), environment: {K: V}, enabled: boolean, timeout: ms (default 5000). Values support {env:VAR} and {file:path}.

Remote (McpRemoteConfig): type "remote", url (required), headers: {K: V}, enabled, timeout, oauth: {clientId, clientSecret, scope, callbackPort (default 19876), redirectUri (default http://127.0.0.1:19876/mcp/oauth/callback)} or false to disable auto-detection. Omitting clientId attempts RFC 7591 dynamic registration.
Disable an inherited server with { "enabled": false } (schema allows the bare {enabled} object).

v2 schema (deprecates the flat map): mcp.servers.<name> with `disabled`, `codemode`, `timeout: {startup, catalog, execution}`, `protocol: legacy|auto|2026-07-28`, and snake_case oauth {client_id, client_secret, scope, callback_port, redirect_uri, auth_server_metadata_url}; mcp.timeout {startup, catalog, execution} global defaults. Not used by the installed 1.18.35 build's docs.

Tool filtering: `tools: { "<server>*": false }` or `"<server>_<tool>": true` globally or inside an agent's `tools`/permission; MCP tool names are prefixed with the server name. Docs warn MCP tools consume context tokens.
CLI: `opencode mcp add [name]`, `opencode mcp list` (alias ls), `opencode mcp auth [name]`, `opencode mcp logout [name]`, `opencode mcp debug <name>`.
Deprecated experimental.mcp_timeout (ms) exists in the schema.

records.summary: Permissions are a map from tool key to allow, ask or deny, optionally with per-pattern objects for input-matching tools. Keys: read, edit, glob, grep, list, bash, task, external_directory, todowrite, question, webfetch, websearch, lsp, doom_loop, skill, plus arbitrary tool names and "*". Patterns use * and ?, ~ or $HOME at the start of path patterns, and the last matching rule wins. Agent permissions merge over global ones. The reviewed docs describe no OS-level sandbox; enforcement is approval prompts, and --auto approves everything not explicitly denied.
details: Values: "allow" (run without approval), "ask" (prompt), "deny" (block). Top-level `permission: "allow"` applies to everything. Per-tool shorthand "allow" equals {"*": "allow"}.

Object form for input-matching keys (read, edit, glob, grep, list, bash, task, external_directory, lsp, skill and custom/MCP tools): e.g. "bash": {"*": "ask", "git *": "allow", "rm *": "deny"}. Rules are evaluated in insertion order and the LAST matching rule wins, so put broad rules first.
Flat-only keys (action string only): todowrite, question, webfetch, websearch, doom_loop.
Defaults per docs: most keys default to allow; doom_loop and external_directory default to ask; read denies *.env and *.env.* but allows *.env.example by default.

external_directory governs paths outside the project worktree; patterns are filesystem paths, e.g. {"~/projects/personal/**": "allow"}. Reference directories (`references` config) are automatically allowed through this boundary.
doom_loop: permission asked when the agent repeats the same tool call pattern (loop detection).
Agent overrides: agent.<name>.permission merges with and takes precedence over global; Plan mode is implemented as the `plan` agent's ruleset (edit: deny).
Legacy `tools: {name: boolean}` is converted to permission allow/deny at load (write/edit/patch -> edit). `experimental.primary_tools` restricts tools to primary agents.

Auto mode: `--auto` on the TUI, `opencode run` and `opencode attach` ("auto-approve permissions that are not explicitly denied (dangerous!)"); explicit deny rules still apply. Plugins can also answer prompts via the permission.ask hook.

v2 schema: `permissions` is an array of {action, resource, effect} rules (Permission.Ruleset) and `policies` is an array of {action: provider.use|tool.use|integration.use, resource, effect: allow|deny}.

Sandboxing: the docs describe only approval-based permissions and the Bun-hosted bash tool; no OS sandbox (seatbelt, bubblewrap, container) is mentioned anywhere in the permissions, config or CLI docs.

records.summary: Sessions, messages and permissions are persisted in a SQLite database under ~/.local/share/opencode. Sessions are listed, continued, forked, exported and imported from the CLI and TUI. Sharing uploads a session to OpenCode's service and yields a public link; `share` config is manual (default), auto or disabled. Context compaction is automatic when the window fills and tunable under `compaction`; plugins can customise the compaction prompt. There is no persistent cross-session memory feature beyond AGENTS.md rules.
details: Storage: `opencode debug paths` prints data ~/.local/share/opencode, state ~/.local/state/opencode, cache ~/.cache/opencode, config ~/.config/opencode. `opencode db path` prints the SQLite path; `opencode db [query] --format json|tsv` opens a sqlite shell. Docs (troubleshooting) still describe the older layout project/<slug>/storage/ for session JSON.

CLI: `opencode session list [-n|--max-count] [--format table|json]`, `opencode session delete <sessionID>`, `opencode export [sessionID] [--sanitize]`, `opencode import <file-or-share-url>`, `opencode stats [--days N] [--tools N] [--models [N]] [--project]`, `opencode --continue|-c`, `--session|-s <id>`, `--fork`.
TUI: /sessions (/resume, /continue), /new (/clear), /undo, /redo (backed by `snapshot` config, default true), /export (Markdown), /compact (/summarize), /share, /unshare.

Share: /share creates a public URL copied to the clipboard; /unshare deletes the remote data. `share`: "manual" (default) | "auto" (every new session shared) | "disabled". `opencode run --share` shares a headless session. Legacy `autoshare: true` maps to share: auto. Docs URL format opncd.ai/s/<share-id>; enterprise options: disabled, SSO-restricted, self-hosted (enterprise.url key).

Compaction config: compaction.auto (default true), compaction.keep.tokens, compaction.buffer; deprecated prune, tail_turns, preserve_recent_tokens, reserved. Env OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT and OPENCODE_DISABLE_PRUNE. Hidden `compaction` agent performs it; plugin hooks experimental.session.compacting and experimental.compaction.autocontinue customise it. Per-provider `settings.compaction.type` summary|native.
tool_output.max_lines (default 2000) and max_bytes (default 51200) control when tool output is truncated to disk under tool-output/.
`warming` keeps recent sessions warm with transient model requests (default false). `username` is shown in conversations and used for telemetry identity.
Sessions can be shared between a headless server and TUI/web clients (`opencode attach <url>`), and the GitHub action and SDK operate on the same session model.

records.summary: Models are addressed as provider_id/model_id (optionally #variant). `model` sets the default and `small_model` the model for titles and similar tasks. The `provider` object adds or overrides providers using an AI SDK npm package, options such as apiKey and baseURL (with {env:} substitution), and a `models` map; the catalog comes from models.dev. Credentials are stored by `opencode auth login` or /connect. Local servers (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp) are added as @ai-sdk/openai-compatible providers, and OpenCode's own gateway is the `opencode` provider (model ids opencode/<model>).
details: Model string pattern in schema: ^[^/#]+\/[^#]+(?:#[^#]+)?$ or object {providerID, model, variant}. Selection precedence: --model/-m flag, config `model`, last used model, first model by internal priority.

ProviderConfig (v1): api, name, env (env var names), id, npm (e.g. "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "@ai-sdk/anthropic"), whitelist, blacklist, options {apiKey, baseURL, headers, enterpriseUrl (GitHub Copilot), setCacheKey, timeout, headerTimeout (default 300000), chunkTimeout (default 300000)}, models {<id>: {id, name, family, release_date, attachment, reasoning, temperature, tool_call, interleaved, cost, limit, options, variants, ...}}.

Per-model `options`: reasoningEffort (OpenAI), thinking {type, budgetTokens} (Anthropic), textVerbosity, reasoningSummary, include. `variants` named option sets; built-in variants: Anthropic high|max, OpenAI none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh, Google low|high; cycled with the variant_cycle keybind (ctrl+t) or `--variant`.

v2 Config.ProviderEncoded: canonical, name, env, package, compatibility {reasoningField, requireReasoning, maxTokensField, requireFinishReason, requireAssistantAfterTool, supportsPromptCacheKey, cacheFormat}, settings {timeout, headerTimeout, chunkTimeout, compaction, transport http|websocket, encoding zstd|gzip|none}, headers, body, models.

Auth: `opencode auth login [--provider|-p] [--method|-m]`, `opencode auth list|ls`, `opencode auth logout`; 1.18.35 CLI names the command `opencode providers` with alias `auth` (subcommands list, login [url], logout [provider]). Credentials saved to ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json. Plugins can add auth methods (AuthHook with oauth/api methods) and dynamic model lists (ProviderHook.models).

records.summary: `opencode run "prompt"` runs one non-interactive turn and can emit raw JSON events with --format json, continue or fork sessions, attach to a running server, run a slash command, or auto-approve permissions. `opencode serve` exposes the full engine as an HTTP API with SSE events, protected by basic auth via OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD; `opencode web` adds a browser UI and `opencode attach` connects a TUI to it. The @opencode-ai/sdk wraps that API, `opencode acp` speaks the Agent Client Protocol for editors such as Zed and JetBrains, and `opencode github` installs and runs a GitHub Actions agent triggered by /opencode or /oc comments.
details: `opencode run [message..]` flags (1.18.35 --help): --command, -c/--continue, -s/--session, --fork, --share, -m/--model, --agent, --format default|json, -f/--file (attach files), --title, --attach <url>, -p/--password, -u/--username, --dir, --port, --variant, --thinking, -i/--interactive, --auto; global --print-logs, --log-level DEBUG|INFO|WARN|ERROR, --pure.

`opencode serve` flags: --port (default 0 = random; docs say 4096 default for SDK), --hostname (127.0.0.1), --mdns (advertises opencode.local, binds 0.0.0.0), --mdns-domain, --cors <origins>. Same flags on `opencode web` and `opencode acp` (acp also --cwd). `server` config object: port, hostname, mdns, mdnsDomain, cors. Auth: OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD enables HTTP basic auth, OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME defaults to "opencode".

API endpoints (docs): GET/POST /session, GET/DELETE /session/:id, POST /session/:id/message, GET /session/:id/message, POST /session/:id/prompt_async, POST /session/:id/command, POST /session/:id/permissions/:permissionID, GET /event and GET /global/event (SSE), GET/PATCH /config, GET /agent, /tui/* for remote-controlling the TUI, /experimental/tool and /experimental/tool/ids (from SDK types), OpenAPI spec at /doc.

SDK: `npm install @opencode-ai/sdk`; createOpencode({hostname, port, signal, timeout, config}) starts server and client; createOpencodeClient({baseUrl: "http://localhost:4096", fetch, parseAs, responseStyle, throwOnError}) connects; methods session.create/list/get/delete/update/messages/message/prompt (with `format` for structured output)/command/shell/abort/share/unshare, config.get, config.providers, app.log, app.agents, global.health, event.subscribe (SSE). Plugins receive the same client as `input.client`.

ACP: `opencode acp` runs OpenCode as a subprocess speaking JSON-RPC over stdio; editors configure command "opencode" args ["acp"]; supported in Zed (ACP registry), JetBrains (acp.json), Avante.nvim, CodeCompanion.nvim; built-in tools, custom tools, slash commands, MCP servers, AGENTS.md, agents and permissions all work; /undo and /redo unsupported.

GitHub: `opencode github install` installs the GitHub app, workflow and secrets; `opencode github run [--event] [--token]` is what the action executes. Action: anomalyco/opencode/github@latest with inputs model (required, provider/model) and agent (primary agent, falls back to default_agent or build); triggered by /opencode or /oc in issue_comment and pull_request_review_comment, plus issues, pull_request, schedule, workflow_dispatch; needs id-token: write and optionally contents/pull-requests/issues: write; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or other provider key) as a secret.

`opencode pr <number>` checks out a GitHub PR branch then starts opencode. `opencode web` opens the browser UI on the server; `opencode attach <url> [--dir] [-c] [-s] [--fork] [-p] [-u] [--mini]` connects a TUI to a running server. Desktop app and `--mini` minimal TUI also exist.

Env for automation: OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD, OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME, OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT (inline config for CI), OPENCODE_PERMISSION (inline permission JSON), OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE, OPENCODE_CLIENT (defaults to "cli").
